compatibility.note: Use the SparkStudio build identified by the workshop bundle or a newer compatible build with the listed features. The original v0.1.0-preview.1 installer predates this catalog's baseline; its version number alone does not establish compatibility.

workshops.title: Scheduled backup workshop
workshops.summary: A read-only checkpoint for encrypted configuration downloads, daily SMB/FTP/FTPS delivery, gateway-specific age retention and isolated restore.
prerequisites: Use the companion scheduling build and an engineering administrator on a disposable gateway; preview.5 predates this feature.
Run tools/load-backup-example.mjs with SPARKSTUDIO_ADMIN_AUTH_FILE to create a new unpublished checkpoint project; --publish is an explicit option. The loader does not change gateway backup settings.
Choose an archive passphrase and a dedicated writable test SMB share or FTP/FTPS directory for the remote exercise. No credentials, remote folders or certificate material are included.
The daily schedule defaults to disabled, 02:00 in the gateway time zone, seven-day retention and a 300-second transfer deadline. Save and verify a manual delivery before enabling it.
Configuration archives exclude live databases, history and audit data. Keep separate database backups and use the offline full-backup procedure when complete stopped-gateway data is needed.
walkthrough: Load the checkpoint screen into the disposable gateway, review and publish SCHEDULE-LAB-A, then save an unpublished SCHEDULE-LAB-B draft.
Open Gateway Settings → Recovery, save an archive passphrase with scheduling disabled, create a download and inspect its configuration scope.
Configure the dedicated destination, deliver a manual backup and verify its success before enabling the daily schedule. Observe an unavailable-destination failure without older-archive deletion.
Review the default 02:00 daily time in the gateway time zone and seven-day retention. Confirm the next run before enabling; change the time deliberately for an isolated scheduled-run exercise.
Restore to a fresh isolated directory, review quarantine and exclusions, and compare published A with draft B before permitting external activity.

workshops.title: Network HTTPS access
workshops.summary: A read-only published application for checking local management, network HTTPS, DNS names and trusted operator access.
features: separate local management and network HTTPS ports
PEM certificate and DNS identity validation
prerequisites: Use the companion network-listener build on a disposable gateway; preview.5 predates these installer choices.
Provide a DNS hostname, matching server certificate and PEM key, client CA trust and the intended firewall rule. No certificate material is included.
Publish the supplied synthetic screen and grant a separate operator account View. No equipment, database, Python actions or external internet is required.
Run tools/load-network-example.mjs on a disposable local gateway with explicit administrator credentials to create its unpublished draft; the loader does not configure listeners.
walkthrough: Install Local only first or choose Network HTTPS with a distinct port, DNS hostname and matching PEM pair.
Create the first administrator through local management, then import/review/publish this project and grant operator View.
Open the operator project from another computer using the trusted HTTPS hostname and inspect the local-only checkbox.
Inspect both actual listeners, then verify a managed upgrade keeps the selected network settings.

workshops.title: Gateway expressions and reviewed tag imports
workshops.summary: Synthetic counts and elapsed time drive a gateway-calculated rate and Boolean limit, with import preview and bad-quality exercises.
prerequisites: Use the companion build with expression tags and an engineering administrator account; public preview 5 predates this example.
The bundled Python runtime and operator Operate permission are needed for the synthetic Save action.
Use tools/load-tag-engineering-example.mjs with SPARKSTUDIO_ADMIN_AUTH_FILE, an unused project name and an unused [default]TagWorkshop namespace on a disposable gateway.
walkthrough: Load into an isolated gateway, inspect the tags, then publish and open the operator application.
Save 20 counts and 30 seconds: observe 40 per minute and a false limit; zero seconds propagates Bad_ExpressionError.
Disable Count and re-enable it. Preview an import, alter a tag, then observe stale-review rejection.

workshops.title: Gateway recovery lab
workshops.summary: Verify an offline encrypted full-gateway backup, isolated restore and explicit restart after review using synthetic data.
prerequisites: Use the companion gateway build with the --recovery CLI on a disposable data directory.
Stop all gateway and external file writers before backup. Keep the original directory and archive passphrase separately.
The lab screen makes no writes; the administrative walkthrough creates backup and restored files. Production gateways and live equipment are excluded.
walkthrough: Publish checkpoint A, then save an unpublished draft B and record synthetic gateway resources.
Stop, back up and inspect the archive. Restore into a new location and verify corrupted copies fail safely.
Start the restored copy on a separate local recovery port and verify connectors, Python and operator APIs are blocked.
Review synthetic destinations, approve and restart; compare the published and draft checkpoints and retained local resources.

workshops.title: Designer diagnostics
workshops.summary: Capture a bounded local snapshot of property failures, resource references, tag quality and retained browser-event messages.
prerequisites: Use the companion build with Project diagnostics and the built-in sample read-query provider.
No equipment, configured tags, external database, assets, Python or external network is required.
The optional deliberate browser-event failure needs administrator-enabled Live actions; default read-only Preview blocks authored scripts.
walkthrough: Enter Preview, set requested width to -1 and enable the invalid-color checkbox. Open Project diagnostics and inspect both Property bindings failures.
Filter for width, open its owner and verify Preview ends with that component selected without editing its definition.
Reenter Preview with valid defaults and refresh the snapshot. The former property errors disappear; Query properties explicitly reports its sample was not captured.
Try the deliberate event checkbox in read-only Preview and inspect the blocked event message. Optionally enable Live actions and repeat to see its authored failure and timestamp.
Inspect Resource references and Tag quality/connection. The example creates no tags; quality records reflect only the current gateway snapshot.

workshops.title: Canvas precision
workshops.summary: Select controls by type, match widths/heights with group-aware bounds and inspect authored grid coordinates.
prerequisites: Use the companion Designer build with Select type, Match size and numeric grid controls.
No tags, assets, scripts, database or external network is required.
walkthrough: Select Rectangle and match width, height and both dimensions; undo each operation.
Select Ellipse and compare the saved group with the independent circle. Match the grouped bounds and undo.
Use Ctrl+Shift+A or Cmd+Shift+A to select the chosen component type. Try grid 12 and then 0; drag while inspecting boundary guides and X/Y/W/H.
Save and publish an accepted arrangement. Runtime bindings remain authoritative over any authored coordinates they control.

workshops.title: Reusable visual styles
workshops.summary: Share appearance across screens and reusable forms while retaining local overrides and binding precedence.
prerequisites: Use the companion build with Visual styles in the Designer Project pane.
No equipment, tags, database, assets, scripts or external network is required.
walkthrough: Edit independent station notes in Preview and compare shared style appearance on both panels.
Change Section caption font size, cancel once, then Apply. The local 30-pixel override stays unchanged until cleared.
Toggle Use attention color: its binding wins while the assigned style still supplies font appearance. The disabled button remains disabled.
Change Station card background and compare Assembly with the Packing local override. Inspect why deleting a referenced style is blocked.
Undo the catalog once, then save and publish an accepted change. Export/re-import to verify stable style assignments.

workshops.title: Preview communication
workshops.summary: Start with gateway-enforced read-only Preview, then deliberately enable temporary draft actions as an administrator.
prerequisites: The built-in sample query needs no external database or configured tags.
The optional screen/template/popup Python message buttons require the bundled Python runtime and an administrator-enabled Live actions session.
Authored browser scripts are also disabled in default read-only Preview; publication has its own operator permission boundary.
walkthrough: Enter Preview and verify Live read-only, editable native local fields, pure bindings, sample query reads and popup navigation.
Try the three Python message buttons: each is blocked in read-only mode.
As a gateway administrator, open Enable live actions, cancel once, then confirm. The form resets and popup closes.
Run the optional screen, nested and popup message actions. They only return messages and do not write gateway data.
Return to read-only and verify the actions are blocked again. Exit and reopen Preview to confirm Live actions is never remembered.

workshops.title: Publication history
workshops.summary: Review and restore an earlier operator snapshot while preserving the current Designer draft.
prerequisites: Use the companion build with Publication history and a user with Publish permission.
No Python runtime, tags, assets, database or external network is required.
This is application snapshot history; separately published libraries/jobs, databases and gateway configuration are outside its restore scope.
walkthrough: Publish Release A, then edit the title to Release B and publish again. Compare the two history entries.
Leave Release C as a draft, review Release A and explicitly restore its operator publication.
Reload the operator application: Release A renders while the Designer retains Release C.
Use another Designer tab to publish while a restore review is open; the stale restore must be rejected.
Export and import the project. Its draft survives, while the new project starts unpublished without local publication history.

workshops.title: Offline caption translations
workshops.summary: Translate component captions through an offline message catalog while preserving live form values and parameter identities.
prerequisites: Use the companion build with Translations and the Preview/operator Language selector.
No database, equipment, tags, assets, scripts or external network is required.
This increment translates captions in en/es/fr/de/it/pt language families; number/date formatting, menu/option labels and RTL layout are separate work.
walkthrough: Enter distinct main and station notes in Preview. Select Spanish and verify captions change while notes, machine parameters and choice values remain unchanged.
Navigate using translated buttons. Select French and inspect the deliberately missing translation with its visible English fallback note.
Add the missing French translation, cancel once, then Apply. Undo restores the catalog in one step.
Inspect reference-protected message deletion and parameter-token validation. Save and explicitly publish an accepted translation.
Open an application-only operator link with ?lang=es. Export/re-import to verify the catalog and authored defaults.

workshops.title: Canvas authoring defaults
workshops.summary: Save starting document sizes and grid spacing without resizing existing screens and templates.
prerequisites: Use the companion build with Canvas authoring defaults in Project settings.
No tags, assets, scripts, database or external network is required.
walkthrough: Inspect the existing 1100 × 680 screen and 300 × 160 template. Their dimensions remain independent of project defaults.
Add a screen and template to inspect the configured 1400 × 900 and 700 × 450 starting sizes; undo each creation.
Edit defaults in Project settings, cancel once, then apply a valid change and undo it.
Save grid 12, change the session toolbar grid to 4, then reopen Designer and verify the saved initial grid returns.
Export/re-import and repeat the new-document checks. Existing geometry stays unchanged.

workshops.title: Gateway operations
workshops.summary: Explore the administrator resource/session console and bounded operational diagnostics using a synthetic application.
features: deployment configuration provenance and observed transport
prerequisites: Use the companion build and a gateway administrator for Gateway Settings in Designer or Settings in Projects.
The project itself needs no tags, assets, database, scripts or external network.
Use only a disposable sign-in for the optional session revocation exercise; it changes that session’s authentication state.
walkthrough: Import and publish the named workshop. Open Gateway Settings and locate its Designer/operator links.
Compare engineering and operator sessions. If testing revocation, identify and revoke only a disposable session, leaving the current and other sessions active.
Open Diagnostics and refresh twice at least one second apart. Inspect CPU, memory, disk and bounded route observations.
Wait over 30 seconds to verify the stale snapshot indicator, then refresh.

Open Deployment. Compare actual listeners, startup values and saved settings. Edit a loopback HTTP port, Validate draft, then Discard draft and reload. Verify the saved revision and actual listeners remain unchanged. Saving/restart/recovery requires the separate disposable-gateway exercise in the guide.
Download and inspect the local support snapshot; it excludes credentials, identities, authored project content and tag values. Ordinary Designer/operator users cannot open the console.

workshops.title: Asset library and replacements
workshops.summary: Review structured image use and preview selective replacements across screens and shared template definitions.
prerequisites: Load the authored fixture into a separate project and bring two local PNG, JPEG or WebP images, each up to 512 KiB.
Upload both images and assign image A to Desk photo, Detail photo and the shared template image before publication. The fixture intentionally contains no image files.
After setup, normal project export produces a portable .sparkproj with the referenced image assets. No tags, database or scripts are required.
walkthrough: Upload two local images, configure the three authored image references and open Asset library.
Search by image name or shared template location and open a listed owning component without editing it.
Preview replacement with image B; select only Desk photo, apply and use one Undo. Other references remain on A.
Replace only the shared template image and compare both placements, then undo.
Save all replacements while the operator stays on its previous publication. Publish explicitly, export and re-import the configured project.

workshops.title: Bulk replacement
workshops.summary: Preview literal text changes across screens and templates, apply selected properties and undo the entire batch.
prerequisites: Use the companion Designer build with Search project → Replace… and the Replace in project dialog.
No configured tags, database, assets, scripts, Python runtime or network access are required.
walkthrough: Preview the local form and navigate between Line A desk and Line A review; compare their shared station cards.
Find Line A and replace with Cell B in Display text. Apply only the desk title and repeated caption; one Undo restores both.
Compare Match case on and off using the Line A / line a / LINE A caption; apply only that row, then Undo.
Replace only the shared template caption and verify both placements before one Undo.
Apply all case-sensitive display-text matches. Inspect unchanged field keys, defaults, option values and navigation IDs, then Undo.
Choose Tag paths and verify the project has no candidates; cancel without changes.
Publish the original project, make a draft replacement and verify the operator title changes only after explicit Save and Publish.

workshops.title: Resource changes
workshops.summary: Preview screen and template renames, inspect deletion blockers, review code-text warnings and undo grouped changes.
prerequisites: Use the companion gateway build with resource change previews.
No configured tags, external database, assets or network access are required.
The optional read-only Python button requires the bundled Python runtime and operator permission.
walkthrough: Edit Station note in Preview and navigate to Station details and back.
Rename Station details and Station card; verify stable IDs preserve navigation and both template placements.
Preview deletion of the connected screen, shared template and Station note input; inspect blockers and cancel.
Delete the scratch label, two-part group and unused Spare card separately, using one Undo after each.
Preview Scratch screen deletion, review and acknowledge the Python comment match, then apply and Undo.
Temporarily configure Scratch screen as startup and a menu item; inspect deletion cleanup, cancel and restore navigation.
Publish the intact workshop, then verify an unpublished draft deletion does not change the operator application.

workshops.title: Project resource search
workshops.summary: Find screens, templates, component properties and query uses; distinguish explicit dependencies from script-text matches.
prerequisites: Use the companion Designer build with Search project. No configured gateway tags or external database is required.
The optional read-only Python button needs the bundled Python runtime and permission to run it.
walkthrough: In Designer, search production-card and inspect its two structured placement references. Open one to select it.
Search production-summary and find the query's explicit uses in the template value and detail table.
Filter Script matches for production-summary. The button comment is searchable text, not a verified query dependency.
Close Production details, then reopen it through search. Edit a caption and find the unsaved text; undo the edit.
Publish and open the operator application. Compare the synthetic production cards, open details and return with Back.

workshops.title: Component properties and form events
workshops.summary: A small order form calculates a total and changes its layout through property bindings and browser input events.
prerequisites: No gateway tags, database, external equipment or Python action is required.
walkthrough: Change Quantity and Unit price; Total recalculates from the current form values.
Edit Order code and commit with Enter or Tab to exercise the browser commit handler.
In Designer, inspect the card's width, text and background bindings and the saved Quantity/Unit price group.

workshops.title: Process displays
workshops.summary: One local reading drives a numeric LED, progress bar, cylindrical tank, level indicator and thermometer.
prerequisites: No configured gateway tags, database, external equipment or Python action is required.
Leave the synthetic [default]ProcessWorkshop/Unavailable path undefined; it deliberately supplies the exercise's unavailable-data case.
walkthrough: Change the local reading and compare the five displays against their authored scales.
Turn off Sample source available to see unavailable data instead of a fabricated zero reading.
Open a display's property sheet to inspect its value, range and formatting bindings.

workshops.title: Process graphics and equipment
workshops.summary: An editable transfer diagram combines pipes, shapes, equipment symbols and an equipment popup.
prerequisites: No configured gateway tags, database, external equipment or Python action is required.
Leave the synthetic [default]Graphics/MissingSignal path undefined; it deliberately supplies the exercise's unavailable-data case.
walkthrough: Toggle Running and Reverse flow, then change Source level to inspect the local process animation.
Turn off Signal available to inspect unavailable-state presentation.
Select pump P-101 to open its details popup; close it and edit a pipe's points in Designer.

workshops.title: Multi-state inputs and indicators
workshops.summary: A segmented mode selector drives a mapped indicator beside an intentionally unmapped state and a masked input.
prerequisites: The bundled Python runtime and operator Operate permission are needed for Preview local form.
Use disposable sample text in the masked field; this workshop is not an authentication form.
No gateway tags, database or external equipment is required.
walkthrough: Choose each requested mode and compare the mapped indicator's text and color.
Inspect the separate unmapped feedback example's unavailable state.
Enter disposable sample text and choose Preview local form. The read-only Python result reports the mode and whether text was entered, without returning that text.

workshops.title: Template properties and typed parameters
workshops.summary: A station form appears once and in saved rows with typed limits, permissions and inherited presentation properties.
prerequisites: The bundled Python runtime and operator Operate permission are needed for the read-only preview buttons.
No gateway tags, database or external equipment is required.
walkthrough: Move the width and position sliders, then toggle form visibility and highlighting.
Change station quantities and compare each station's limit and permission; Station C is read-only.
Preview an allowed quantity and inspect the typed parameter definitions on the shared template.

workshops.title: Nested forms and saved rows
workshops.summary: Nested equipment cards, repeated saved rows and contextual popups keep form inputs in their own containing instance.
prerequisites: The bundled Python runtime and operator Operate permission are needed for read-only submission previews.
No gateway tags, database or external equipment is required.
walkthrough: Edit one equipment card's setpoint and acknowledgement; the other card keeps its own draft.
Preview an allowed inner form and inspect its returned inputs and typed parameters.
Open a contextual inspection popup and compare its independent note with the saved-row screen's separate forms.

workshops.title: Template parameter expressions
workshops.summary: A machine choice and batch quantity drive nested parameter expressions while saved rows retain their own identities.
prerequisites: The bundled Python runtime and operator Operate permission are needed for read-only submission previews.
No gateway tags, database or external equipment is required.
walkthrough: Change Machine and Batch quantity; the nested form resolves the parent quantity and the card's extra quantity.
Type a local note, then change Machine to observe the dependent form reset.
Preview a resolved form and open a saved row's inspection popup to check that its machine context remains independent.

workshops.title: Session and screen state
workshops.summary: A station desk, review screen and inspection popup demonstrate shared session choices and fresh screen-local counters.
prerequisites: No gateway tags, database, external equipment or Python action is required.
walkthrough: Choose a station and target, then open Review; the session choices carry across screens.
Toggle the review checkbox, leave and return to see its screen counter start fresh.
Open, close and reopen inspection; each popup owns a new local counter while session choices remain shared.

workshops.title: Two-way input state bindings
workshops.summary: Mirrored inputs across root and nested forms share typed state while local invalid drafts and screen notes remain isolated.
prerequisites: The bundled Python runtime and operator Operate permission are needed for read-only submission previews.
No gateway tags, database or external equipment is required.
walkthrough: Change either quantity input or the nested form and check that accepted values reach the other bound controls.
Leave an invalid numeric draft in one form; the accepted shared value remains unchanged and that form cannot submit it.
Open Review and the inspection popup to compare session values with independent notes, then reset the workshop defaults.

workshops.title: Private template instance state
workshops.summary: Side-by-side and repeated equipment panels each own private quantities, notes and reset behavior.
prerequisites: The bundled Python runtime and operator Operate permission are needed for read-only submission previews.
No gateway tags, database or external equipment is required.
walkthrough: Edit a panel's quantity and mirrored field; only that instance's private values change.
Edit the nested note, reset one panel and compare its state with the neighboring panel and saved rows.
Open and reopen inspection to see fresh popup state, then preview a form to inspect only its validated local fields.

workshops.title: State-driven template parameters
workshops.summary: Session station, screen batch and each panel's private extra quantity feed reusable forms directly through parameter bindings.
features: state sources in template parameter bindings
prerequisites: The bundled Python runtime and operator Operate permission are needed for read-only submission previews.
No gateway tags, database or external equipment is required.
walkthrough: Change Session station and Screen batch; the reusable forms receive updated typed parameters.
Change Private extra quantity in one panel or saved row and compare its independent result with the other instances.
Open state inspection and change Popup batch; its opening context stays captured while its current quantity follows fresh popup state.

workshops.title: Component lifecycle and property events
workshops.summary: Independent panels distinguish user edits from observed property changes and demonstrate popup cleanup and bounded failures.
prerequisites: No gateway tags, database, external equipment or Python action is required.
The diagnostics screen intentionally produces timeout and feedback-loop errors; return to the panels or restart Preview to reset the demonstration.
walkthrough: Edit Quantity and then assign 7 from a script; compare User edit events with Property events.
Open and close lifecycle inspection and check that cleanup writes remain zero.
Open the diagnostics lab, run the timeout test before the loop test, and verify bounded failures leave navigation available.

workshops.title: Named-query property bindings
workshops.summary: A built-in synthetic read query drives reusable panels, numeric values, geometry, color and visibility with explicit error cases.
features: query bindings in templates and popups
prerequisites: The built-in sample query provider is required; no external database or connection setup is needed.
The bundled Python runtime and operator Operate permission are needed only for the explicit Refresh query data button.
No gateway tags or external equipment is required.
walkthrough: Choose Line 1 and Line 2; the selected panel and geometry change while the comparison panel retains Line 2.
Choose Missing line or All lines to see unavailable scalar results, then restore a valid line.
Open inspection and examine a property's Named query fx editor in Designer. Run preview explicitly to inspect the selected column and transform.

workshops.title: Read query operations
workshops.summary: A synthetic SQLite project demonstrates typed parameters, read deadlines, cancellation and recovery.
prerequisites: Use a disposable gateway with an administrator and create the declared managed SQLite connection/database using the guide. Project packages do not carry database files or connections.
Load the three named reads and workshop screen as described in the guide; no Python runtime, external equipment or SQL Server is needed.
Run the intentionally slow read only from Designer. The operator table uses the fast records query.
walkthrough: Set up the synthetic SQLite database, load the workshop and explicitly publish its draft.
Run Typed quantity with minimum 45, then invalid text; verify invalid typed values fail before database execution.
Run Slow read with a 1-second deadline, then with 30 seconds and Cancel read query. No cancelled result should appear.
Run Production records again and open the operator screen. The three synthetic records remain available; no update query was executed.

workshops.title: Operator form with memory-tag persistence
workshops.summary: An operator form explicitly saves a shift name, target rate, mode and enabled flag into synthetic gateway memory tags.
prerequisites: Set up the four synthetic [default]Application memory tags declared in the source fixture; .sparkproj does not carry tag definitions or values.
The bundled Python runtime and operator Operate permission are required to save settings.
Use the authenticated development loader on an isolated gateway; it adds resources to the default project.
walkthrough: Load the example after reviewing its tag definitions and Python save action.
Enter a shift name, target rate, mode and enabled state, then choose Save settings.
Compare the saved-value displays with the form and reopen it to read the persisted memory-tag values.

workshops.title: Operator input components
workshops.summary: A text area, spinner, slider, radio group, date/time input and toggle save explicit synthetic work-order values.
prerequisites: Set up the six synthetic [default]InputWorkshop memory tags declared in the source fixture; these gateway resources are not in a project package.
The bundled Python runtime and operator Operate permission are required for the save action.
Use the authenticated development loader on an isolated gateway; it adds resources to the default project.
walkthrough: Load the declared synthetic tags and input screen, then edit each input type.
Run the save action and compare quantity, rate and enabled feedback with the edited values.
Inspect the date/time input as a local wall-clock string and the numeric limits in each property sheet.

workshops.title: Expression bindings with a tag permit
workshops.summary: Local form expressions drive text, color and visibility while one synthetic memory tag gates a read-only Python action.
prerequisites: Create the declared Boolean memory tag [default]BindingWorkshop/Permit; the loader creates it only if absent.
The example's Python action only returns form values; the gateway write is the initial memory-tag setup.
The bundled Python runtime and operator Operate permission are needed for Apply quantity.
walkthrough: Use the authenticated loader on an isolated gateway to add the permit tag and screen.
Change Quantity and Show details to observe the caption, color and visibility expressions.
Inspect Apply quantity's Enabled binding, then run its read-only Python preview when the permit and form conditions allow it.

workshops.title: Reusable workcenters and order cards
workshops.summary: Two workcenter forms and saved-row order cards use parameterized tag paths and explicit memory-tag save actions.
prerequisites: Set up the twelve synthetic Workcenters and Orders memory tags declared in the source fixture; project packages do not include them.
The bundled Python runtime and operator Operate permission are required for save and release actions.
Use the authenticated development loader on an isolated gateway; it adds resources to the default project. Author navigation between its two regular screens if needed.
walkthrough: Edit and save one workcenter; compare its persisted target and mode with the other instance.
Open Order board in Designer Preview, choose a sample order priority and explicitly release that order.
Edit the shared workcenter template and inspect how each instance supplies its machine parameter.

workshops.title: Local images and contextual popups
workshops.summary: A bundled local drawing leads to workcenter and order dialogs that retain the main screen's draft context.
prerequisites: Load the authored examples/assets/assembly-cell.png asset and the eight synthetic Workcenters and Orders memory tags declared in the source fixture.
Images can be carried by .sparkproj, but its memory-tag definitions and values require separate gateway setup.
The bundled Python runtime and operator Operate permission are required for popup save and release actions.
walkthrough: Use the authenticated development loader on an isolated gateway to add its image, tags and project resources.
Enter a shift note, open a workcenter popup and save a changed target; closing the popup retains the main screen note.
Open a saved order's details, change its priority and explicitly release only that synthetic order.

workshops.title: SQLite lists, trees and tables
workshops.summary: Synthetic SQLite records drive query-backed list and tree selections, table paging and independent station forms.
features: connection test history, dependencies and enable/disable
prerequisites: Use tools/load-data-controls-example.mjs with authenticated administrator access on an isolated development gateway. It creates a separate project, sqlite-data-controls connection and data-controls.db with synthetic production_records.
The reserved project name, connection ID and database path must be unused; the loader refuses existing configured resources and publishes the new project immediately.
The bundled Python runtime and operator Operate permission are needed for read-only form previews. Runtime actions do not update the database.
walkthrough: Run the dedicated setup loader and open the newly created Data workshop operator application.
Select a list item, tree item or table row to fill the local form; page, sort and filter the loaded table result.

On the isolated gateway only, test Data workshop SQLite and inspect the saved time plus draft/published query dependencies. Disable and save it, verify reads fail, then re-enable, save and test again. Changing the connection invalidates its earlier test result.
Preview the selected form values, then open Independent station forms to compare isolated list and tree choices.
